editorial:
Imagine going back to your old childhood house to help your sick dad, only to find an old toy you thought you left behind years ago. That is exactly what happens here. You follow a woman who is already stressed out and sad, and things get weird fast when her old stuffed puppy starts showing up in places it shouldn't be. It starts off feeling like a sad family story, but it quickly turns into a scary ride. You will feel the tension build up as you realize that this toy is not just fabric and stuffing, but something much more dangerous that wants to bring back a terrible memory from her past.

The acting is top-notch and makes you really care about the characters. The pacing is great because it doesn't rush the scares, though some parts in the middle might feel a bit slow for some. If you like movies that make you question what is real, you will love this. You should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the creepy details, or if you are a collector, grab the 4K Blu-ray for your shelf. It is a wild ride that stays with you long after the credits roll.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you discover the puppy toy was actually holding the spirit of the daughter's younger brother who died years ago. He was not trying to kill her, but was trying to warn her that their father caused the accident. The twist is that the father is the real villain. In the end, the woman burns the toy and the house down to stop the cycle of pain and finally escape her father's lies.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and scary toys.
